chapter_text:
CHAPTER 19 — पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः (PUTRO'HAM PRITHIVYAH)

Introduction — भूमिसूक्तम् किम्?

One of the oldest and most beautiful expressions of love for nature anywhere in the world is found in the अथर्ववेद (Atharvaveda). Its twelfth book opens with a long hymn of sixty-three verses addressed to the Earth herself. This hymn is called the भूमिसूक्तम् (Bhumi-suktam, 'the Hymn to the Earth') or पृथ्वीसूक्तम् (Prithvi-suktam). In it the seer (ऋषि) does not treat the Earth as mere soil or property. He speaks to her as a living mother — नमस्करोति, he bows to her, praises her mountains and rivers, her forests and fields, and asks her forgiveness for every wound that human work causes her. The single line that gives this lesson its title, 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' ('The Earth is my mother, and I am the son of the Earth'), is the heart of the whole vision. In this chapter (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we read a few public-domain verses of the भूमिसूक्त together with a famous nature-सुभाषित, learn their word meanings (शब्दार्थ), translate them into simple English, draw out their message of reverence and environmental care, and use them to learn a little Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्).

Why the Earth-Mother idea matters (मातृभावः पृथिव्याः)

In the Indian tradition the Earth is not a dead thing to be used up. She is भूमिमाता / धरित्री / वसुन्धरा — the patient bearer of all beings. Because she 'holds' (धारयति) and 'nourishes' (पुष्णाति) every creature, she is naturally seen as a mother, and every human being as her child (पुत्रः / सन्तानः). Once we accept that relationship, the way we treat the land, the water, the trees and the animals changes completely. We do not loot a mother; we serve her, thank her, and take from her only what we truly need. The ancient seer therefore joins two ideas that our own age is only now rediscovering: गौरवम् (reverence) and संरक्षणम् (conservation). To feel that 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' is at once a spiritual feeling and a practical rule of environmental ethics (पर्यावरण-नीतिः).

Selected verses (शब्दार्थ सहित)

1) यत्ते मध्यं पृथिवि यच्च नभ्यं यास्त ऊर्जस्तन्वः सम्बभूवुः ।
   तासु नो धेह्यभि नः पवस्व माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः ।
   पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु ॥ (अथर्ववेद १२.१.१२)
   शब्दार्थ: यत् = which; ते = your; मध्यम् = middle; पृथिवि = O Earth (सम्बोधन); च = and; नभ्यम् = navel, central part; याः = which (feminine plural); ऊर्जः = nourishing sap, strength; तन्वः = bodies, forms; सम्बभूवुः = have arisen/come together; तासु = in those; नः = us, to us; धेहि = place, grant; अभि नः पवस्व = purify us; माता = mother; भूमिः = the Earth; पुत्रः = son; अहम् = I; पृथिव्याः = of the Earth; पर्जन्यः = the rain-cloud / rain-god; पिता = father; सः = he; उ = indeed; पिपर्तु = may he nourish / fill / protect.
   Translation: O Earth, that which is your middle and your navel, and the nourishing powers (ऊर्ज) that have arisen from your body — set us amid those and purify us. The Earth is (my) mother, and I am the son of the Earth; Parjanya, the giver of rain, is (my) father — may he nourish us.
   Message: This is the theme verse. The seer names the Earth 'mother' and himself her 'son', and the rain-cloud 'father'. Mother Earth and Father Sky together feed all life; the child's duty is gratitude and care.

2) यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु ।
   मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम् ॥ (अथर्ववेद १२.१.३५)
   शब्दार्थ: यत् = whatever; ते = of you, from you; भूमे = O Earth (सम्बोधन); विखनामि = I dig out; क्षिप्रम् = quickly; तत् = that; अपि = also; रोहतु = may it grow again; मा = not (prohibition); मर्म = vital / tender point; विमृग्वरि = O purifying one (address to the Earth); हृदयम् = heart; अर्पिपम् = may I injure / pierce.
   Translation: O Earth, whatever I dig out of you, may it quickly grow again; O purifier, may I not strike your vital part, may I not wound your heart.
   Message: A remarkable early rule of environmental ethics. Even while farming, mining or building, the human being asks the Earth's pardon and prays that what is taken will be renewed and that she will not be permanently harmed. Take, but do not wound; use, but let it grow back.

3) सत्यं बृहदृतमुग्रं दीक्षा तपो ब्रह्म यज्ञः पृथिवीं धारयन्ति ।
   सा नो भूतस्य भव्यस्य पत्न्युरुं लोकं पृथिवी नः कृणोतु ॥ (अथर्ववेद १२.१.१)
   शब्दार्थ: सत्यम् = truth; बृहत् = the great; ऋतम् = the cosmic / moral order; उग्रम् = the mighty (law); दीक्षा = consecration, discipline; तपः = austerity; ब्रह्म = sacred knowledge / prayer; यज्ञः = sacrifice; पृथिवीम् = the Earth; धारयन्ति = (they) uphold, support; सा = she; नः = for us; भूतस्य = of what has been (the past); भव्यस्य = of what will be (the future); पत्नी = mistress, queen; उरुम् = wide, spacious; लोकम् = world, room; कृणोतु = may (she) make.
   Translation: Truth, the great cosmic order, the mighty (law), consecration, austerity, sacred prayer and sacrifice uphold the Earth. May she, the mistress of what has been and what shall be, make wide room for us.
   Message: The Earth is upheld not by force alone but by सत्य (truth) and ऋत (right order). A world kept in balance by truth and duty will in turn 'make wide room' for its children. Ecology and ethics are joined.

4) दश कूपसमा वापी दश वापीसमो ह्रदः ।
   दश ह्रदसमः पुत्रो दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः ॥ (a well-known nature-सुभाषित, cf. मत्स्यपुराण)
   शब्दार्थ: दश = ten; कूप = a well; समा = equal to; वापी = a large step-well / water-tank; ह्रदः = a lake; पुत्रः = a son; द्रुमः = a tree.
   Translation: One वापी (large tank) equals ten wells; one lake equals ten वापीs; one (worthy) son equals ten lakes; and a single tree equals ten sons.
   Message: A famous verse in praise of planting trees and digging water-bodies. To plant one tree is called a greater गुण (merit) than to have ten sons — so precious is a tree to the Earth and to all beings. Serving nature is serving the family of life.

भावविस्तारः — Gratitude and care (कृतज्ञता एवं संरक्षणम्)

When we read these verses together, a single teaching shines through. Because the Earth is our mother (माता), three feelings naturally follow. First, गौरवम् (reverence): we bow to her, we do not treat her as mere dirt. Second, कृतज्ञता (gratitude): every grain of food, every drop of water, every breath of air is her gift, so we give thanks. Third, संरक्षणम् (protection): a good child does not harm the mother, so we protect her forests (वनानि), rivers (नद्यः) and creatures (प्राणिनः). The famous prayer 'मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि' asks pardon before we even lift a spade. In our own century, when pollution (प्रदूषणम्), deforestation (वननाशः) and climate change threaten all life, this ancient vision has become urgent practical wisdom. To plant a tree, to save water, to keep the air and rivers clean, to be gentle to animals — these are the modern ways of saying 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः', 'I am a child of the Earth'.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the verses (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). When two sounds meet in Sanskrit they often combine and change; splitting them back (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill.
  • पुत्रः + अहम् → पुत्रोऽहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि: अः before अ becomes ओ, and the following अ is elided and marked by the sign अवग्रह ऽ). This is the very word in our title.
  • हृदयम् + अर्पिपम् → हृदयमर्पिपम् (म् joins the following vowel). Split back as हृदयम् + अर्पिपम्.
  • यत् + ते → यत्ते (juxtaposed त्, doubling of the sound). Split as यत् + ते.
  • वापी + समः → वापीसमः; ह्रद + समः → ह्रदसमः (compound joins).
  • तत् + अपि → तदपि (त् softens to द् before a vowel, व्यञ्जन-सन्धि). Split as तत् + अपि.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). Sanskrit nouns change their ending to show their role. From our verses:
  • सम्बोधन (vocative, calling): पृथिवि 'O Earth', भूमे 'O Earth', विमृग्वरि 'O purifier'.
  • प्रथमा (nominative, the subject): माता 'mother', भूमिः 'the Earth', पुत्रः 'son', पर्जन्यः 'the rain-god', पिता 'father', द्रुमः 'tree'.
  • द्वितीया (accusative, the object): पृथिवीम् 'the Earth (as object)', उरुम् लोकम् 'wide room', हृदयम् 'heart'.
  • षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): पृथिव्याः 'of the Earth', भूतस्य 'of the past', भव्यस्य 'of the future'.
  • सप्तमी (locative, 'in/among'): तासु 'in those (powers)'.

(C) शब्दरूप (declension of a noun — worked examples). भूमि is a feminine noun ending in इ. Its प्रथमा (nominative) runs: एकवचन भूमिः, द्विवचन भूमी, बहुवचन भूमयः; its षष्ठी एकवचन is भूमेः. पृथिवी is a feminine noun ending in ई: प्रथमा पृथिवी / पृथिव्यौ / पृथिव्यः, and its षष्ठी एकवचन is पृथिव्याः — exactly the form in 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः'.

(D) धातुरूप (verb forms). Two useful verbs appear. रुह् (to grow) gives रोहति in लट् (present) and रोहतु in लोट् (imperative, 'let it grow'): लोट् प्रथमपुरुष रोहतु / रोहताम् / रोहन्तु — this रोहतु is the very word in verse 2. धृ (to hold/uphold) gives धारयति (present, singular) and धारयन्ति (present, plural, 'they uphold') as in verse 3. The imperative कृणोतु ('may she make') and पिपर्तु ('may he nourish') are also लोट् forms of prayer.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you met the अथर्ववेद भूमिसूक्त — the world's oldest great hymn to the Earth — and its central line 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः', 'the Earth is my mother, I am the son of the Earth'. You read four public-domain verses: the theme verse naming Earth as mother and rain as father; the environmental-ethic verse 'यत्ते भूमे विखनामि... मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्' asking the Earth's pardon before digging; the verse that सत्य and ऋत uphold the Earth; and the सुभाषित that one tree equals ten sons. For each you studied the शब्दार्थ, an English translation and the message. You then drew grammar from the verses: विसर्ग-सन्धि in पुत्रोऽहम्, the vocative and other विभक्ति, the शब्दरूप of भूमि and पृथिवी (giving पृथिव्याः), and the धातुरूप रोहतु / धारयन्ति. The heart of the lesson is a feeling and a duty together: to revere the Earth as a mother, thank her for all she gives, and protect her — for पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः, I am a child of the Earth.

It introduces the अथर्ववेद भूमिसूक्त and its central line 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' (the Earth is my mother, I am her son), presents public-domain verses with their meanings and message of reverence, gratitude and environmental care, and draws simple grammar — सन्धि, विभक्ति, शब्दरूप and धातुरूप — from the verses.

sections.heading: The Earth Hymn and its vision
bullets: The भूमिसूक्त / पृथ्वीसूक्त is a hymn of sixty-three verses to the Earth in the twelfth book of the अथर्ववेद — one of the world's oldest nature poems.
It treats the Earth (भूमि / पृथिवी / धरित्री / वसुन्धरा) not as dead soil but as a living mother who holds (धारयति) and nourishes all beings.
Its central line, 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः', declares the Earth to be the mother and the human being her son — the source of both reverence and conservation.

sections.heading: The Earth as mother and rain as father
bullets: In AV 12.1.12 the seer prays to be set amid the Earth's nourishing powers and says: माता भूमिः, पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः — Earth is mother, I am her son.
पर्जन्यः पिता — Parjanya, the rain-cloud, is the father; Mother Earth and Father Sky together feed all life.
Accepting the Earth as mother makes gratitude and gentle use of her gifts a natural duty.

sections.heading: Environmental awareness and gratitude
bullets: यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु — whatever is dug from the Earth should be allowed to grow back.
मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम् — a prayer not to wound the Earth's vital part or heart, an early rule of environmental ethics.
The सुभाषित 'दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः' — one tree equals ten sons — praises planting trees and digging water-bodies.
Today this means planting trees, saving water, reducing pollution and being gentle to animals.

sections.heading: Sandhi from the verses
bullets: विसर्ग-सन्धि: पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम् (अः before अ becomes ओ; the elided अ is marked by अवग्रह ऽ).
व्यञ्जन-सन्धि: तत् + अपि = तदपि (त् softens to द् before a vowel).
सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting a joined form back into its words) is a key reading skill.

sections.heading: Vibhakti, shabda-rupa and dhatu-rupa
bullets: सम्बोधन (vocative): पृथिवि, भूमे, विमृग्वरि — 'O Earth', 'O purifier'.
प्रथमा माता / भूमिः / पुत्रः (subject); द्वितीया पृथिवीम् / हृदयम् (object); षष्ठी पृथिव्याः / भूतस्य (of); सप्तमी तासु (in).
शब्दरूप: भूमि (प्रथमा भूमिः / भूमी / भूमयः); पृथिवी (षष्ठी एकवचन पृथिव्याः).
धातुरूप: रुह् → रोहतु (लोट्, 'let it grow'); धृ → धारयन्ति (present, 'they uphold').

key_takeaways: The भूमिसूक्त of the अथर्ववेद is a great hymn to the Earth; its heart is 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' — the Earth is my mother and I am her son.
Because the Earth is our mother, we owe her reverence (गौरवम्), gratitude (कृतज्ञता) and protection (संरक्षणम्).
यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु — take from the Earth, but let what is taken grow back; do not wound her heart.
सत्य and ऋत uphold the Earth (पृथिवीं धारयन्ति); ecology and ethics go together.
One tree is worth ten sons (दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः) — planting trees and saving water are acts of love for the Earth.
विसर्ग-सन्धि gives पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम्; splitting it is सन्धि-विच्छेद.
पृथिव्याः is the षष्ठी (genitive) 'of the Earth'; रोहतु is लोट् of रुह् and धारयन्ति is the present plural of धृ.

glossary.definition: The 'Hymn to the Earth' — a hymn of sixty-three verses in the twelfth book of the अथर्ववेद praising the Earth as mother; also called पृथ्वीसूक्तम्.
The Earth; in this lesson revered as माता (mother) who holds and nourishes all beings.
Mother; the Earth is addressed as माता, the source of nourishment for all life.
Son / child; 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' means 'I am the son (child) of the Earth'.
'Of the Earth' — the षष्ठी (genitive) singular of पृथिवी, as in पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः.
The rain-cloud or rain-god; called पिता (father), the giver of rain that, with Mother Earth, feeds all life.
'May it grow (again)' — लोट् (imperative) of the root रुह् (to grow), from यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु.
A vital or tender point; the seer prays not to strike the Earth's मर्म — an early rule of not harming nature.
'(They) uphold / support' — present tense (plural) of धृ; सत्य, ऋत and others uphold (धारयन्ति) the Earth.
A tree; the सुभाषित says one द्रुम (tree) equals ten sons, praising the planting of trees.
The environment / surroundings; caring for पर्यावरण (forests, water, air) is the modern form of 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः'.
Protection / conservation; a good child protects the mother, so we protect the Earth's forests, rivers and creatures.
Gratitude; thankfulness to the Earth for food, water and air — a central feeling of the hymn.
The sign ऽ that marks an elided अ after ओ/ए in विसर्ग-सन्धि, e.g. पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + अहम्.
The vocative case of address ('O ...'); पृथिवि, भूमे and विमृग्वरि are सम्बोधन forms calling upon the Earth.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 19)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate into simple English:
माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः।
पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु॥
questions.answer: The Earth (भूमि) is (my) mother, and I am the son (पुत्र) of the Earth (पृथिव्याः). Parjanya (the rain-cloud, पर्जन्य) is (my) father — may he nourish/protect us (नः पिपर्तु).
questions.explanation: The theme verse names Earth as mother, the speaker as her son, and rain as father.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: माता, भूमिः, पुत्रः, पर्जन्यः, पिता.
questions.answer: माता = mother; भूमिः = the Earth; पुत्रः = son; पर्जन्यः = the rain-cloud / rain-god; पिता = father.
questions.explanation: These words come from the theme verse (AV 12.1.12).

questions.question: In one or two sentences, explain the environmental message of 'यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु, मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्'.
questions.answer: It teaches that whatever we dig or take from the Earth should be allowed to grow back quickly, and that we must not wound the Earth's vital point or heart. The message is to use nature's resources gently and gratefully, without permanently harming her.
questions.explanation: An early rule of environmental ethics — take, but do not wound.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) पुत्रोऽहम् (b) हृदयमर्पिपम्.
questions.answer: (a) पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + अहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि: अः + अ = ओ + ऽ). (b) हृदयमर्पिपम् = हृदयम् + अर्पिपम् (म् joins the following vowel).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its role for each word: पृथिवि, पृथिव्याः, पृथिवीम्.
questions.answer: पृथिवि = सम्बोधन (vocative) → 'O Earth' (calling). पृथिव्याः = षष्ठी (genitive) → 'of the Earth'. पृथिवीम् = द्वितीया (accusative) → 'the Earth' as object.
questions.explanation: सम्बोधन calls, षष्ठी shows 'of', द्वितीया marks the object.

questions.question: Explain the idea 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः'. Why is the Earth called a mother, and how can a student live by this idea today?
questions.answer:
The line means 'the Earth is my mother, and I am the son of the Earth'. The Earth is called a mother (माता) because, like a mother, she holds (धारयति) and nourishes (पुष्णाति) every living being — she gives us food, water, air and a place to live, expecting nothing in return. If she is our mother, we are all her children (पुत्राः), and this makes reverence (गौरवम्), gratitude (कृतज्ञता) and care (संरक्षणम्) our natural duty.
A student can live by this idea today by planting and protecting trees, saving water and electricity, not littering or polluting rivers and air, being kind to animals and birds, and encouraging others to keep the surroundings clean. Just as a good child never harms his mother, we should never harm the Earth. To feel 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' turns environmental care from a rule into a loving family duty.
questions.explanation: Earth-as-mother reasoning plus practical modern environmental actions.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (2-3 lines) in Devanagari about protecting nature (प्रकृति-संरक्षणम्). Give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. भूमिः अस्माकं माता अस्ति। (The Earth is our mother.)
2. वयं वृक्षान् रोपयामः। (We plant trees.)
3. जलं न दूषयेम। (We should not pollute the water.)
Together these say: the Earth is our mother, so we plant trees and do not pollute water — we care for nature as her children.
questions.explanation: Simple प्रथमा-subject sentences using chapter vocabulary; verbs अस्ति, रोपयामः, दूषयेम.

questions.question: Translate 'दश ह्रदसमः पुत्रो दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः' and state its moral.
questions.answer: Translation: A (worthy) son (पुत्र) equals ten lakes (ह्रद), and a single tree (द्रुम) equals ten sons. Moral: A tree is of immense worth — planting even one tree is a great act of merit and service to the Earth and all beings.
questions.explanation: The सुभाषित praises the planting of trees above even having sons.

questions.question: Read 'सत्यं बृहदृतमुग्रं दीक्षा तपो ब्रह्म यज्ञः पृथिवीं धारयन्ति'. What upholds the Earth, and what does the verse's message suggest?
questions.answer: According to the verse, truth (सत्य), the great cosmic order (ऋत), consecration (दीक्षा), austerity (तप), sacred prayer (ब्रह्म) and sacrifice (यज्ञ) uphold (धारयन्ति) the Earth. The message is that the Earth is held up not by force but by truth and right order — so ecology and ethics are joined.
questions.explanation: The verse links the stability of the Earth to सत्य and ऋत.

questions.question: What is the भूमिसूक्त, and give two reasons why it is important?
questions.answer: The भूमिसूक्त (पृथ्वीसूक्त) is a hymn of sixty-three verses to the Earth found in the twelfth book of the अथर्ववेद. Two reasons it is important: (1) it is one of the world's oldest expressions of love and reverence for the Earth, seeing her as a living mother; (2) it teaches an early environmental ethic — to take from the Earth gently and let what is taken grow back — which is deeply relevant to today's care for nature.
questions.explanation: Definition (source, Earth-hymn) plus its cultural and environmental value.

questions.question: The भूमिसूक्त (Hymn to the Earth) belongs to the अथर्ववेद.
questions.explanation: It is the great hymn opening the twelfth book of the अथर्ववेद.

questions.question: In the hymn the Earth is treated as lifeless soil with no worth.
questions.explanation: The Earth is revered as a living mother (माता).

questions.question: In the theme verse, पर्जन्य (the rain-cloud) is called the father (पिता).
questions.explanation: पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु.

questions.question: 'क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु' wishes that what is dug from the Earth should grow back quickly.
questions.explanation: रोहतु = 'may it grow'; क्षिप्रम् = quickly.

questions.question: 'द्रुमः' means a river.
questions.explanation: द्रुम = a tree; नदी = a river.

questions.question: 'मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्' expresses a wish to harm the Earth as much as possible.
questions.explanation: It is a prayer NOT to wound the Earth (मा...अर्पिपम्).

questions.question: Planting trees and saving water are modern ways of living by 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः'.
questions.explanation: Caring for the Earth is what a good child of the Earth does.

questions.question: पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम् is an example of विसर्ग-सन्धि.
questions.explanation: अः + अ → ओ + ऽ (the elided अ marked by अवग्रह).

questions.question: 'पृथिव्याः' is the षष्ठी (genitive) case meaning 'of the Earth'.
questions.explanation: षष्ठी एकवचन of पृथिवी = पृथिव्याः, 'of the Earth'.

questions.question: 'माता भूमिः' means 'the Earth is my enemy'.
questions.explanation: It means 'the Earth is (my) mother'.

questions.question: The Hymn to the Earth is called the भूमि____ (name of the hymn type).
questions.explanation: भूमि + सूक्तम् = भूमिसूक्तम्, the Hymn to the Earth.

questions.question: Complete: 'माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं ____ ।'
questions.explanation: माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः.

questions.question: Complete: 'यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि ____ ।'
questions.explanation: ...क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु — may it grow again.

questions.question: Complete: 'पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः ____ ।'
questions.explanation: पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु — may he nourish us.

questions.question: Complete: 'दश ह्रदसमः पुत्रो दश पुत्रसमो ____ ।'
questions.explanation: ...दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः — a tree equals ten sons.

questions.question: In the theme verse the Earth is the माता and the human being is her ____ (Sanskrit word).
questions.explanation: पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः — I am her son.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'माता' = ____ (English).
questions.explanation: माता = mother.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'पिता' = ____ (English).
questions.explanation: पिता = father.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'द्रुमः' = ____ (English).
questions.explanation: द्रुम = a tree.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: 'हृदयम्' = ____ (English).
questions.explanation: हृदय = heart.

questions.question: सन्धि: पुत्रः + अहम् = ____.
questions.explanation: विसर्ग-सन्धि: अः + अ = ओ + ऽ.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: पुत्रोऽहम् = ____ + अहम्.
questions.explanation: पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम्.

questions.question: सन्धि: हृदयम् + अर्पिपम् = ____.
questions.explanation: म् joins the following vowel.

questions.question: विभक्ति: 'पृथिव्याः' is in the ____ (case name in English).
questions.explanation: षष्ठी / genitive = 'of the Earth'.

questions.question: Translate 'भूमिः' into English: ____.
questions.explanation: भूमि = the Earth.

questions.question: What is the भूमिसूक्त, and in which Veda is it found?
questions.answer: The भूमिसूक्त (also called पृथ्वीसूक्त) is a hymn of sixty-three verses in praise of the Earth. It is found in the twelfth book (काण्ड) of the अथर्ववेद, and it addresses the Earth as a living mother.
questions.explanation: Definition and source of the hymn.

questions.question: Why does the seer of the भूमिसूक्त call the Earth a mother?
questions.answer: Because the Earth, like a mother, holds (धारयति) and nourishes (पुष्णाति) every living being — she gives food, water, air and a place to live to all creatures without asking anything in return. This motherly giving makes her माता and every being her child.
questions.explanation: Earth as nourisher = mother.

questions.question: Write the theme line of the lesson (about mother and son) in Devanagari.
questions.explanation: Recall of the title line (AV 12.1.12).

questions.question: Write the first line of the verse about not wounding the Earth (यत्ते भूमे...) in Devanagari.
questions.answer: यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु।
questions.explanation: Recall of the environmental-ethic verse (AV 12.1.35).

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' in one sentence.
questions.answer: It means 'the Earth (भूमि) is my mother (माता), and I am the son (पुत्र) of the Earth (पृथिव्याः)' — the human being is a child of Mother Earth.
questions.explanation: Whole-line meaning.

questions.question: Explain the message of the verse 'यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु, मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्'.
questions.answer: The seer says to the Earth: whatever I dig out of you, may it quickly grow again (क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु); O purifying Earth, may I not strike your vital point (मर्म) nor wound your heart (हृदय). The message is that human beings must take from the Earth gently and gratefully, letting what is used be renewed, and must never permanently harm her. It is an early and beautiful rule of environmental care.
questions.explanation: Take but do not wound; let it grow back.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: भूमिः, पृथिव्याः, पर्जन्यः.
questions.answer: भूमिः = the Earth; पृथिव्याः = of the Earth; पर्जन्यः = the rain-cloud / rain-god.
questions.explanation: Word meanings from the theme verse.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: विखनामि, रोहतु, मर्म.
questions.answer: विखनामि = I dig out; रोहतु = may it grow (again); मर्म = a vital / tender point.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the environmental verse.

questions.question: State and briefly explain the environmental message of the सुभाषित 'दश कूपसमा वापी... दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः'.
questions.answer: The verse ranks things by their worth: a large water-tank (वापी) is worth ten wells, a lake ten tanks, a worthy son ten lakes, and — highest of all — a single tree (द्रुम) is worth ten sons. Its message is that planting trees and making water-bodies are acts of the highest merit, because trees and water sustain all life. It urges us to protect and increase greenery and water sources as a sacred duty to the Earth.
questions.explanation: Value of trees and water; conservation.

questions.question: Name three practical ways a student can act as a 'child of the Earth' (पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः).
questions.answer: A student can: (1) plant and protect trees and keep the surroundings green; (2) save water and electricity and avoid littering or polluting; (3) be kind to animals and birds and encourage others to keep rivers and air clean. These acts show reverence, gratitude and care for Mother Earth.
questions.explanation: Practical environmental actions.

questions.question: 'A factory dumps waste into a river to save money.' Using the ideas of the lesson, say whether this is right and why.
questions.answer: It is wrong. The lesson teaches 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' — the Earth is our mother and we are her children, so we owe her reverence (गौरवम्), gratitude (कृतज्ञता) and protection (संरक्षणम्). The verse 'मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्' asks us not to wound the Earth. Dumping waste to save money wounds the river and harms all creatures who depend on it, which is exactly what the hymn forbids. The right course is to treat the waste and protect the water, even at some cost, because caring for the mother comes before profit.
questions.explanation: Applies non-harm and Earth-as-mother to a modern case.

questions.question: Translate into English: 'सत्यं ... पृथिवीं धारयन्ति'.
questions.answer: 'Truth (सत्य) ... uphold(s) the Earth (पृथिवीं धारयन्ति)' — that is, truth and the cosmic order (along with discipline, austerity, prayer and sacrifice) hold up and sustain the Earth.
questions.explanation: Simple translation of the key phrase.

questions.question: Translate the theme verse phrase 'यास्त ऊर्जस्तन्वः सम्बभूवुः, तासु नो धेहि' and explain it.
questions.answer: It means 'the nourishing powers (ऊर्जः) which have arisen (सम्बभूवुः) as your bodies/forms — set us (धेहि) amid those (तासु)'. The seer prays that Mother Earth may place her children in the midst of her life-giving, nourishing energies so that they may be strong and well fed.
questions.explanation: Translation plus meaning of the prayer for nourishment.

questions.question: Translate 'यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु' and name the message in one phrase.
questions.answer: 'O Earth, whatever I dig out of you, may it quickly grow again.' Message in one phrase: use nature's resources but let them be renewed (sustainable, non-harmful use).
questions.explanation: Translation + one-line message.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) पुत्रोऽहम् (b) तदपि.
questions.answer: (a) पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + अहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि: अः + अ = ओ + ऽ). (b) तदपि = तत् + अपि (त् softened to द् before the vowel).
questions.explanation: Splitting joined forms.

questions.question: Join by sandhi: (a) हृदयम् + अर्पिपम् (b) पुत्रः + अहम्.
questions.answer: (a) हृदयम् + अर्पिपम् = हृदयमर्पिपम् (म् joins the vowel). (b) पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम् (अः + अ = ओ + ऽ).
questions.explanation: Sandhi joins.

questions.question: What is the sign ऽ called, and what does it show? Give one example.
questions.answer: The sign ऽ is called अवग्रह. It shows that a short अ has been elided (dropped) after ओ or ए in विसर्ग-सन्धि. Example: पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + अहम्, where the अ of अहम् is elided and marked by ऽ.
questions.explanation: अवग्रह marks an elided अ.

questions.question: Give the विभक्ति (case) and role of: (a) पृथिवि (b) पृथिव्याः.
questions.answer: (a) पृथिवि = सम्बोधन (vocative) — calling, 'O Earth'. (b) पृथिव्याः = षष्ठी (genitive), singular — 'of the Earth'.
questions.explanation: Vocative vs genitive.

questions.question: Write the शब्दरूप of भूमि in प्रथमा विभक्ति (all three numbers).
questions.answer: प्रथमा: एकवचन भूमिः, द्विवचन भूमी, बहुवचन भूमयः.
questions.explanation: Declension of the feminine इ-stem भूमि, nominative.

questions.question: From which धातु is 'रोहतु' formed, in which लकार, and what does it mean?
questions.answer: रोहतु is formed from the धातु रुह् (to grow). It is in the लोट् लकार (imperative), third person singular, and means 'may it grow / let it grow'.
questions.explanation: धातुरूप of रुह् in लोट्.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु'.
questions.answer: It means 'Parjanya (the rain-cloud) is (our) father; may he indeed nourish/protect us (नः पिपर्तु)'. Just as Mother Earth feeds us from below, Father Rain feeds us from above, and the seer prays for his nourishing care.
questions.explanation: Rain as father who nourishes.

questions.question: Which verse would you quote to persuade people to plant more trees, and why?
questions.answer: I would quote 'दश ह्रदसमः पुत्रो दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः' — a single tree is worth ten sons. It shows that in our tradition planting even one tree is counted as a very great merit, so it powerfully encourages people to grow and protect trees.
questions.explanation: Applies the tree-सुभाषित.

questions.question: What is the भूमिसूक्त? Explain its source, its vision of the Earth, and why it is important.
questions.answer:
The भूमिसूक्त (पृथ्वीसूक्त) is a great hymn of sixty-three verses addressed to the Earth, found in the twelfth book of the अथर्ववेद. It is one of the oldest and most beautiful nature-poems in the world.
Its vision is that the Earth is not lifeless soil or mere property but a living mother (माता). The seer bows to her, praises her mountains, rivers, forests and fields, and even asks her pardon for the wounds that human work causes her. The central line 'माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' declares the Earth to be the mother and the human being her son.
The hymn is important for several reasons: (1) it is an ancient and moving expression of love and reverence for the Earth; (2) it joins spiritual feeling (Earth as mother) with a practical rule of care (do not wound the Earth); and (3) at a time of pollution and climate change, its message of gratitude and conservation is deeply relevant. For all these reasons it holds a treasured place in Sanskrit literature.
questions.explanation: Source + vision + importance of the hymn.

questions.question: Write any TWO verses (or verse-lines) from the lesson in Devanagari and state the message of each.
questions.answer:
1. माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः। पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु॥ — Message: the Earth is our mother and rain our father; together they nourish us, so we owe them love and gratitude.
2. यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु। मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्॥ — Message: whatever we take from the Earth should grow back, and we must never wound her — an early rule of environmental care.
questions.explanation: Recall of two verses + their messages.

questions.question: Take the verse 'माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः, पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु'. Give its word meanings and full explanation.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: माता = mother; भूमिः = the Earth; पुत्रः = son; अहम् = I; पृथिव्याः = of the Earth; पर्जन्यः = the rain-cloud / rain-god; पिता = father; सः = he; उ = indeed; नः = us; पिपर्तु = may (he) nourish / protect.
Explanation: In this verse the seer states the deepest relationship between a human being and nature. The Earth (भूमि) is addressed as the mother, and the speaker calls himself her son (पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः). The rain-cloud, Parjanya, is called the father, and the seer prays that he may nourish and protect all of us (स उ नः पिपर्तु). Thus Mother Earth (who holds and feeds us from below) and Father Rain (who feeds us from above) together sustain all life. Because they are our parents, we owe them reverence, gratitude and care — and this is the very foundation of environmental awareness.
questions.explanation: Word meanings + Earth-mother / rain-father explanation.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of the following eight words from the verses: माता, पुत्रः, पृथिव्याः, पर्जन्यः, विखनामि, रोहतु, मर्म, द्रुमः.
questions.answer: माता = mother; पुत्रः = son; पृथिव्याः = of the Earth; पर्जन्यः = the rain-cloud / rain-god; विखनामि = I dig out; रोहतु = may it grow (again); मर्म = a vital / tender point; द्रुमः = a tree.
questions.explanation: Consolidated vocabulary from the verses.

questions.question: Discuss how the idea 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' can guide environmental care today. Give at least three practical examples.
questions.answer:
'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः' means 'I am a child of the Earth'. Once we truly feel this, protecting the environment stops being a mere rule and becomes a loving family duty — just as a good child never harms his mother, we never harm the Earth. The verses give the reasons: the Earth is our mother (माता भूमिः); whatever we take should grow back (क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु); we must not wound her heart (मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्); and a single tree is worth ten sons (दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः).
Practical examples today: (1) Plant and protect trees and green spaces, and avoid needless cutting of forests. (2) Save water, keep rivers, lakes and ponds clean, and harvest rain-water. (3) Reduce pollution — use less plastic, avoid dumping waste, save electricity, and keep the air clean. In addition, being gentle to animals and birds and teaching others these habits spreads the same care. Each such act is a modern way of honouring Mother Earth and living out 'पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः'.
questions.explanation: Links the theme to concrete environmental action.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद with three examples taken from the verses of this chapter, naming the type where you can.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its separate words. Examples from the verses:
1. पुत्रः + अहम् = पुत्रोऽहम् (विसर्ग-सन्धि: अः + अ = ओ, and the elided अ is marked by अवग्रह ऽ).
2. हृदयम् + अर्पिपम् = हृदयमर्पिपम् (the म् joins directly with the following vowel).
3. तत् + अपि = तदपि (व्यञ्जन-सन्धि: the hard त् softens to द् before a vowel).
Being able to both join (सन्धि) and split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) these forms is essential for reading Sanskrit verses correctly.
questions.explanation: Definition + three worked examples with types.

questions.question: Using words from the verses, explain the सम्बोधन, प्रथमा, द्वितीया and षष्ठी विभक्ति with one example each, and give the शब्दरूप of भूमि in प्रथमा.
questions.answer:
1. सम्बोधन (vocative, calling 'O...'): पृथिवि / भूमे = 'O Earth'.
2. प्रथमा (nominative, the subject): माता 'mother', भूमिः 'the Earth', पुत्रः 'son'.
3. द्वितीया (accusative, the object): पृथिवीम् 'the Earth (as object)', हृदयम् 'heart'.
4. षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): पृथिव्याः 'of the Earth', भूतस्य 'of the past'.
शब्दरूप of भूमि (feminine इ-stem), प्रथमा: एकवचन भूमिः, द्विवचन भूमी, बहुवचन भूमयः. Recognising these endings helps us see who does what in a verse.
questions.explanation: Four cases with verse examples + declension of भूमि.

questions.question: Translate the verse 'यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु, मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्' and explain it.
questions.answer:
Translation: 'O Earth (भूमे), whatever I dig out of you (यत्ते विखनामि), may it quickly grow again (क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु); O purifying one (विमृग्वरि), may I not strike your vital point (मा ते मर्म), may I not wound your heart (मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्).'
Explanation: Even while farming, mining or building, the human being pauses to ask the Earth's pardon. He prays that what he takes will be renewed and that he will cause no lasting injury to her. The verse is a remarkable early statement of environmental ethics: we may use the Earth's resources, but gently, gratefully and without wounding her.
questions.explanation: Translation + explanation of the non-harm ethic.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer the questions:
माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः।
पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु॥
(a) Who is called the mother? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'पर्जन्यः'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'पृथिव्याः'? (d) State the message.
questions.answer: (a) The Earth (भूमि) is called the mother. (b) पर्जन्यः = the rain-cloud / rain-god. (c) पृथिव्याः is षष्ठी (genitive) — 'of the Earth'. (d) Message: the Earth is our mother and rain our father; together they nourish all life, so we owe them reverence and care.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: meaning, word, case and message.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु।
मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्॥
(a) What does the seer wish about whatever he digs? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'मर्म'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'हृदयमर्पिपम्'. (d) What is the message?
questions.answer: (a) He wishes that whatever he digs from the Earth should quickly grow again (क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु). (b) मर्म = a vital / tender point. (c) हृदयमर्पिपम् = हृदयम् + अर्पिपम्. (d) Message: take from the Earth gently and let it be renewed; never wound her — an early rule of environmental care.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with a sandhi split.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
दश कूपसमा वापी दश वापीसमो ह्रदः।
दश ह्रदसमः पुत्रो दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः॥
(a) What is said to equal ten sons? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'वापी'. (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'द्रुमः'. (d) What value does the verse teach?
questions.answer: (a) A single tree (द्रुम) is said to equal ten sons. (b) वापी = a large step-well / water-tank. (c) द्रुमः = a tree. (d) Value: planting trees and making water-bodies are acts of the highest merit; we should protect and grow greenery and water sources.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the value of trees and water.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
यत्ते भूमे विखनामि क्षिप्रं तदपि रोहतु।
मा ते मर्म विमृग्वरि मा ते हृदयमर्पिपम्॥
(a) Does the verse allow us to use the Earth's resources? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'रोहतु'. (c) What does the seer pray NOT to do? (d) How does this apply to mining or farming today?
questions.answer: (a) Yes — the seer does dig (विखनामि) from the Earth, so using resources is allowed. (b) रोहतु = may it grow (again). (c) He prays NOT to strike the Earth's vital point (मर्म) or wound her heart. (d) Today it means: mine and farm, but do it sustainably — restore the land, let forests and soil recover, and avoid permanent damage.
questions.explanation: Comprehension applied to sustainable use.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer:
माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः।
(a) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'पुत्रोऽहम्'. (b) Name the type of सन्धि. (c) What is the sign ऽ called? (d) Translate the whole line.
questions.answer: (a) पुत्रोऽहम् = पुत्रः + अहम्. (b) It is विसर्ग-सन्धि (अः + अ = ओ). (c) The sign ऽ is called अवग्रह. (d) Translation: 'The Earth is (my) mother, and I am the son of the Earth.'
questions.explanation: Comprehension focused on sandhi and translation.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
सत्यं बृहदृतमुग्रं दीक्षा तपो ब्रह्म यज्ञः पृथिवीं धारयन्ति।
सा नो भूतस्य भव्यस्य पत्न्युरुं लोकं पृथिवी नः कृणोतु॥
(a) What upholds the Earth? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'पृथिवीम्'? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'धारयन्ति'. (d) What does the Earth do for us?
questions.answer: (a) Truth (सत्य), the cosmic order (ऋत), consecration, austerity, sacred prayer and sacrifice uphold the Earth. (b) पृथिवीम् is द्वितीया (accusative), the object of धारयन्ति. (c) धारयन्ति = '(they) uphold / support'. (d) She, mistress of past and future, makes wide room (उरुं लोकं कृणोतु) for us.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with case identification.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
माता भूमिः पुत्रो अहं पृथिव्याः।
पर्जन्यः पिता स उ नः पिपर्तु॥
(a) Who is called the father? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'पिपर्तु'. (c) Translate 'माता भूमिः'. (d) What is the central relationship shown?
questions.answer: (a) Parjanya (the rain-cloud, पर्जन्य) is called the father. (b) पिपर्तु = 'may (he) nourish / protect'. (c) 'माता भूमिः' = 'the Earth is (my) mother'. (d) Central relationship: the human being is the child of Mother Earth and Father Rain.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the family-of-nature idea.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
दश कूपसमा वापी दश वापीसमो ह्रदः।
दश ह्रदसमः पुत्रो दश पुत्रसमो द्रुमः॥
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दश'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'ह्रदः'. (c) What equals ten wells? (d) What is the overall theme?
questions.answer: (a) दश = ten. (b) ह्रदः = a lake. (c) One वापी (large water-tank) equals ten wells. (d) Overall theme: the great worth of trees and water-bodies, and the merit of creating and protecting them.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: vocabulary and theme.

questions.question:
Read the line and answer:
यास्त ऊर्जस्तन्वः सम्बभूवुः तासु नो धेह्यभि नः पवस्व।
(a) What have arisen as the Earth's forms? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'तासु'. (c) What does the seer ask the Earth to do? (d) What feeling does the prayer express?
questions.answer: (a) The nourishing powers (ऊर्जः) have arisen as the Earth's bodies/forms (तन्वः). (b) तासु = 'in those' (locative plural). (c) He asks the Earth to set him amid those nourishing powers (तासु नो धेहि) and to purify him (अभि नः पवस्व). (d) The prayer expresses trust in and gratitude to Mother Earth for nourishment and purity.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the prayer for nourishment.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer:
'The भूमिसूक्त of the अथर्ववेद addresses the Earth as a living mother. Its line माता भूमिः पुत्रोऽहं पृथिव्याः has become a great message of reverence for nature.'
(a) In which Veda is the भूमिसूक्त? (b) How does the hymn regard the Earth? (c) What is another name for the भूमिसूक्त? (d) Why is this hymn important today?
questions.answer: (a) The भूमिसूक्त is in the अथर्ववेद. (b) It regards the Earth as a living mother (माता), not as lifeless soil. (c) Another name is पृथ्वीसूक्त. (d) It is important today because its reverence for the Earth and its call to take from her without harm are exactly the environmental awareness the modern world needs.
questions.explanation: Comprehension on the hymn's source, vision and relevance.
